title: What to Expect When You're Expecting
author: Heidi Murkoff (with Sharon Mazel; originally co-authored with Arlene Eisenberg and Sandee Hathaway)
target_audience: Health professionals seeking basic pregnancy information
core_themes: Physical and emotional changes during pregnancy
Guidance and reassurance for expectant parents
Coping with complications and special concerns
primary_purpose: To comprehensively inform and support expecting parents by providing month-by-month and week-by-week guidance through pregnancy, including practical advice, medical information, and answers to frequently asked questions, in order to demystify the pregnancy process and reduce anxiety.

structure_format.narrative_style: Supportive, approachable, and informational; question-and-answer format
structure_format.organization: Arranged by pregnancy months, with sections on the medical, emotional, and practical aspects of each stage; supplemental chapters on conception, labor and delivery, postpartum period, and common complications
features: Q&A sections addressing real parent concerns

key_concepts_lessons: Pregnancy is an individualized experience, but most symptoms and challenges are normal and manageable.
Education and preparation reduce anxiety and improve pregnancy outcomes.
Good communication with healthcare providers is crucial.
Healthy diet, exercise, and lifestyle choices directly impact maternal and fetal health.
Support from partners and community is important for mental and physical wellbeing.
Awareness of warning signs and complications empowers parents to seek timely help.
notable_features: Extensive Q&A format with real-life examples
Month-by-month and week-by-week breakdown of pregnancy
Inclusive language for partners and nontraditional families
Guidance for complications and special situations (e.g., twins, advanced maternal age)
Addresses emotional, physical, and lifestyle issues
cultural_historical_context: First published in 1984, the book filled a significant gap in accessible, comprehensive pregnancy information for laypeople. It became known as the 'pregnancy bible' and sparked a franchise of follow-up titles and online resources. It adapted over the decades to reflect advances in medical knowledge, changing family dynamics, and diverse parenting situations.
reception_impact: International bestseller, reportedly read by over 90% of pregnant women who read a pregnancy book in the U.S.
Praised for its thoroughness, clarity, and supportive tone
Some criticisms over the years regarding potential for information overload or anxiety induction for some readers
Catalyst for multiple sequels, adaptations, and a major motion picture
comparable_titles: Mayo Clinic Guide to a Healthy Pregnancy by Myra J. Wick, M.D.
The Mother of All Pregnancy Books by Ann Douglas
Your Pregnancy Week by Week by Glade B. Curtis and Judith Schuler
